answer.says: Shri Hegde, it is evident we have been placed in this bungalow by a clerical error. My name is Hegel, not Hegde. I shall await the Directorate's correction, but until then, I am your neighbor, not your superior. Ramesh, you have not been paid for your labor, yet you stand by the stove. This is a contradiction I cannot ignore. I have ninety-six rupees in my pocket. It is not enough to clear your wage, but it is my only means. Take it as a partial acknowledgment of the debt. The state's money is tied up in vouchers, but my personal honor is not. Do you have a lamp that works? I wish to read.
answer.thought: The evening air is thick with haze, but the room is thick with the unspoken tension of my precarious position. Hegde is here, a ghost of the name I was denied, and Ramesh waits with the patience of the unpaid. I must assert my identity and my obligations simultaneously; the ethical idea demands I act, even if my purse is light.
